question.problem: Consider the function $g(x,y)=\frac{{e}^{y}}{yx}.$ What is the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=⟨2,4⟩?$
question.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction of $v$ is equal to the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,1).$ 

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5} \\ u & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}⟨2,4⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the gradient $∇g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{y}}{yx}),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{e}^{y}}{yx})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{{e}^{y}}{{x}^{2}y},\,\frac{{e}^{y}(y-1)}{x{y}^{2}}⟩ \\ ∇g(1,1) & =⟨-\frac{{e}^{1}}{{1}^{2}\cdot 1},\,\frac{{e}^{1}\cdot (1-1)}{1\cdot {1}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-e,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =∇g(1,1)\cdot u \\  & =⟨-e,0⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨1,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(-e\cdot 1+0\cdot 2) \\  & =-\frac{e}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =-\frac{e\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
